sections.h2: Which Mount Vernon offices handle a Rockcastle County tax account?
sections.html:
The work is divided among three counters near the courthouse. The Property Valuation Administration values parcels and answers at (606) 256-4194, using P.O. Box 977, Mt. Vernon, KY 40456 as its mailing address. The sheriff bills and collects from 205 E. Main St., Box 2, at (606) 256-2032. The County Clerk, at (606) 256-2831 and Box 6 in the same building, takes over once a bill goes delinquent.

No one of the three sets a rate. The Rockcastle County Fiscal Court helps, meeting on each month's second Tuesday at 1:00 p.m. in the courthouse, and a resident who wants to be heard asks for a slot 24 hours ahead. The school board and the special districts choose their own levies, and the sheriff bills the sum.

The county says every official record of its government is filed with the County Clerk, which makes that office the first stop for a deed or a lien search. The Fiscal Court also runs an occupational tax office at (606) 256-8374 for employers.

sections.h2: Which dates matter on a Rockcastle County tax bill?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 makes December 31 the due date and names the sheriff as the collector. Unless a delayed mailing moves the county to a shifted calendar, the stages run in this order:

  • Up to November 1: pay the whole bill and keep a 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 to December 31: only the printed figure is owed.
  • All of January: 5 percent is added.
  • From February: 10 percent is added, plus a sheriff's fee that Department of Revenue examples include.
  • April 15: collection ends and the sheriff passes the leftovers to the clerk, with a lien attached.

The shifted calendar gives a month for the discount, a month at face value and a month at 5 percent. The bill itself shows which one applies. Because values are fixed on January 1, a closing in late winter normally leaves the prior year's bill in the seller's name, so request a payoff figure from the sheriff before the closing day.

sections.h2: What might a Rockcastle County home cost to carry?
sections.html:
Frankfort cut its 2025 real estate rate to 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessment. Census QuickFacts puts a typical Rockcastle County house at $123,600, so the state's cut of that is about $131.02. School, county and district rates sit above it, and only the sheriff's bill for a given address shows the sum.

Older and disabled owners receive a deduction that shrinks the base. Take $49,100 away and $74,500 remains, which lowers the state cut to about $78.97. On a house this size the deduction removes a big share of the value, so a qualifying owner gains by filing at the PVA early.

A sale changes the picture. The tax follows whoever held the parcel on January 1, so the contract should assign the year in writing and any open balance should be paid at closing.

sections.h2: What steps does a Rockcastle County appeal follow?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA office, since a conference with the PVA or a deputy must come before any appeal. Staff must explain the law, the procedure and the method behind your number, and a written record keeps your claimed value and the result.

  1. Look for the published notice of the inspection period. The roll opens on May's first Monday and stays open thirteen days.
  2. Meet the PVA in that window, or sooner if an assessment notice has already arrived.
  3. Lodge the appeal at the clerk's office on the workday that follows the end of inspection.
  4. Appear before the local board, which convenes roughly a month after inspection.

The board weighs only what is shown in front of both the PVA and the owner or authorized agent. Insurance papers, construction costs, listings and property descriptions qualify as proof, and a case without them fails. If the board sets a number above yours after bills are out, a supplemental bill arrives.

sections.h2: Which Rockcastle County owners get a tax break?
sections.html:
People aged 65 and over, and people whose total disability is recognized by a federal or retirement program, can claim the homestead deduction on the home they occupy. For 2025 and 2026 it is $49,100. The PVA takes the application and wants a document that shows age, such as a license or passport.

An age claim stays in force while the original applicant keeps living there. Disability claims are renewed yearly unless the owner is a service-connected disabled veteran or has a permanent finding from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. A couple counts as one claimant, and a buyer must file separately because the break is tied to the owner.

Churches, schools, charities and governments may be exempt altogether under sections 170 and 171 of the Kentucky Constitution, after an application to the PVA.

sections.h2: What do unpaid Rockcastle County taxes turn into?
sections.html:
Delinquency begins when business closes on April 15. The sheriff sends the list to the County Clerk, each bill becomes a certificate of delinquency, and a lien described in KRS 134.420 lasts eleven years even after the house is sold.

Interest accrues at 1 percent per month, and clerk and county attorney commissions come next. In the state's sample, a $1,000 bill reaches $1,254.00 at transfer and $1,611.30 after the county attorney's first notice. The sale must fall 90 to 135 days after transfer. A notice goes out 30 days ahead of it, a second can follow, and the clerk advertises the sale for at least 30 days.

A certificate buyer at the sale can add costs. A payment to the sheriff before April 15 keeps the number small.

sections.h2: How do Rockcastle County's housing figures look?
sections.html:
The county came into being in 1810 and borrowed its name from the Rockcastle River, which took it from the river's cliffs. Mount Vernon is the seat and the biggest town, with Brodhead and Livingston as the other communities, and Mount Vernon dates to 1789. About 317 square miles of land lie inside the line, partly within the Daniel Boone National Forest. The county is part of the Richmond-Berea micropolitan area and borders Garrard, Madison, Lincoln, Jackson, Pulaski and Laurel counties.

The 2020 census recorded the whole population as rural, with a median age of 44.1. Commutes average 26.4 minutes, and 80 percent of households subscribe to broadband. A house with repairs pending or a tax lien outstanding can go to a direct cash buyer, with the lien cleared at closing.

faqs.q: Where does a Rockcastle County tax payment go?
faqs.a: To the sheriff's office at 205 E. Main St., Box 2, Mount Vernon, (606) 256-2032. The PVA at (606) 256-4194 only assesses and does not collect.

faqs.q: What does paying early save in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: Two percent of the bill, if it is paid in full by November 1 on the regular schedule. After that only the printed amount is due until year end, and penalties start in January.

faqs.q: What is the older owner deduction in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, taken off the assessed value. Owners who are 65 or over, or totally disabled, apply through the PVA.

faqs.q: When can I speak to the Rockcastle County Fiscal Court?
faqs.a: At its monthly meeting on the second Tuesday, 1:00 p.m., in the courthouse. Give 24 hours of notice to be placed on the agenda.

faqs.q: What if my Rockcastle County bill is still open after April 15?
faqs.a: It moves to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency carrying a lien. Interest of 1 percent monthly starts, and clerk and attorney commissions are added.
